info.text:
Grocery inflation cooled. Your bill didn't.
BLS food-at-home prices: +11.8% in 2022, then +1.3% in 2023 (December to December). Slower, but still up.
From Dec 2019 to Dec 2025, groceries rose about 31%: a $100 cart became about $131.
Cooling inflation means prices rise more slowly; when prices actually fall, that's deflation, which is rare for groceries. Grocery prices were up 2.2% in the 12 months to Aug 2026.
Source: BLS Consumer Price Index.
News and education, not financial advice.
